stem: Faiz wants a fair comparison of two household liquids using one prepared red-rose extract as the indicator. He has a dropper and may later label samples acid or base.

parts.text: Which plan makes that comparison fair?

options.text: Use the same rose extract for both, add comparable amounts of each liquid with a dropper, and record the colour changes.
Use one drop of sample A and ten drops of sample B; the test is still fair if the indicator is the same.
If both samples can later be labelled acid or base, the comparison must have been fair no matter how unequal the amounts were.

parts.text: Give one reason for your choice.

part_answers.answer: A fair test keeps the indicator and amounts comparable so colour differences come from the liquids.

teacher.key_rationale: Fair natural-indicator tests use the same extract and comparable amounts; unequal drops or later labels alone do not make the test fair.
